LLM_description:
Situation:
A severe storm system has disrupted ground lines of communication across the region. Flooding and landslides have severed primary highways, and secondary roads are intermittently passable. Aviation assets are restricted by weather and airspace deconfliction. The 3rd Relief Battalion is coordinating deliveries from multiple logistics nodes, including Supply Depot Bravo (port-based), Depot Charlie (railhead), Depot Delta (air cargo hub), Depot Echo (central warehouse), and Depot Foxtrot (fuel farm). Priority receiving elements are Forward Operating Base Alpha, the Central Field Hospital, the West IDP Collective Center, and the East Rural Clinics network. Several corridors remain hazardous or require engineering support; some urban segments are under curfew control.

Mission:
Deliver life-sustaining commodities (e.g., water, rations, medical supplies, and fuel) from available depots to the priority receiving elements within the current operational window, minimizing total operational cost while mitigating security risk and respecting inventory and fleet constraints. Unmet demand is to be avoided; if unavoidable, it will be tracked and penalized.

Execution/Concept:
- Depot constraints: Each depot’s outbound shipments are limited by its available inventory by supply class. No depot may dispatch more of any item than it holds.
- Demand fulfillment: Each receiving element has a critical requirement by supply class that must be met today. Shortfalls (slack) are permissible only as a last resort and will incur penalty costs to reflect humanitarian impact.
- Vehicle assignment and capacity: Deliveries move via direct depot-to-unit routes using a shared fleet. The total loaded volume on any depot-to-unit movement cannot exceed the number of vehicles assigned to that leg multiplied by per-vehicle capacity. Supply classes differ in volumetric footprint, constraining how much can be loaded per vehicle.
- Route activation and risk: Activating any depot-to-unit route (i.e., sending at least one vehicle on that corridor) triggers a fixed Risk Cost for that route, representing security overhead such as escorts, route clearance, and movement control. This fixed risk outlay applies once per active route within the period, regardless of how many vehicles subsequently use it. Additional vehicles on an already active route incur only their variable transport and vehicle costs.
- Fleet cap: The total number of deployed vehicles across all routes cannot exceed the fleet available. Vehicles cannot move on a route unless that route is activated.
- Cost minimization: The plan minimizes the sum of:
  • Variable transport costs for moving supplies along each route,
  • Shortage penalties for any unmet demand by supply class and unit,
  • Vehicle deployment costs,
  • Fixed route security risk costs for activated routes.
- Operational approach: Consolidate shipments on fewer, safer corridors where feasible to avoid multiple route activations. Prioritize routes with lower risk and transport expense while matching depot inventories to unit demand profiles. Where route risk is high, weigh the fixed activation cost against projected shortage penalties. Allocate vehicles to maximize load utilization given supply volumes and avoid breaching the fleet cap. Maintain flexibility to redirect from disrupted corridors and to stage from alternative depots as inventories allow.
